clue.text: Kitty, given tip, has to go out briefly

parts.note: a kitty is a cat
a nap is a racing tipster's most confident tip

explanation.surface: A cat, given a pointer, has to step outside for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' here means drop off to sleep, not leave the house. NAP is a racing term: the horse a tipster is surest of.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze for a short spell is to drop off, or go out like a light, for a little while.

clue.text: One a record height above a star

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece written above another comes before it

parts.note: A can stand for one, as in a single item
LP is a long-playing record
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone once set a record height, climbing above a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' is a link word joining 'One' to 'record'.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in a constellation is designated by the first Greek letter, so Alpha Centauri is a star.

clue.text: Wrestling hold on boy like Horatio

parts.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold applied under the opponent's arm
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad applies a wrestling hold, much as Horatio would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word: in a down clue the second piece sits on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to Admiral Horatio Nelson, the British naval hero.

clue.text: Notorious sort of relations

definitions.meaning: widely known, out in the open
PR, the work of managing an organisation's image

explanation.surface: A scandalous kind of family connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notorious is widely known, and the press office's work is called public relations.

clue.text: Barriers producing bitter complaints

explanation.surface: Fences that set off angry protests.
explanation.definitionFit: Fences made of rails are barriers, and to rail is to complain bitterly.

clue.text: Descriptive of caddie's work — and figure ure?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Descriptive of caddie's work — and figure ure?': 'ure' is OCR garble and the scan is unreadable, so the exact printed clue cannot be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Descriptive of caddie's work — and figure ure?

clue.text: Run study in diversification for business

indicators.note: letters put through a diversification are varied and spread out into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Running a study into diversifying a firm's interests.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is fodder; 'in diversification' is the anagram signal. Shuffle R, STUDY and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry is commercial activity, the world of trade and manufacturing, so it means business.

clue.text: Gold Stick in revived parliamentary style? Not half!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only half of the word is wanted, its first three letters

parts.note: the Palace of Westminster is built in Gothic Revival style

explanation.surface: Gold Stick, a royal official, in the revived parliamentary style? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: Gold Stick is a court officer, but here 'Gold stick' is a bar of gold. 'Not half!' is British slang for 'definitely', recast as the halving signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar or block of cast gold is a stick-shaped piece of the metal.

clue.text: Grating bolts signifying traffic jams

parts.note: a grid is a grating of bars
locks fasten as bolts do

explanation.surface: A grating fitted with bolts stands for blocked roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Total jams where crossing streets block one another are called gridlock.

clue.text: After short period, certain to appear hypnotised

indicators.note: the second word is placed after the first

parts.note: a spell is a short period of time
bound means sure, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: After a short while, someone is sure to look mesmerised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held as if under a spell is entranced, as though hypnotised.

clue.text: Composer short of energy but still a lively type

indicators.note: lacking something, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: Edvard Grieg, the Norwegian composer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A composer, low on energy, is somehow still a lively soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but still' is a link. A grig is an old word for a merry, lively person.
explanation.definitionFit: Grig is a dated word for a lively, cheerful person, as in 'merry as a grig'.

clue.text: Kinky opera did get taken off

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A kinky operatic production was mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or send them up, which is what a parody does.

clue.text: Take up residence to get a seat

definitions.meaning: a long wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Moving in so as to get a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to make one's home somewhere, and a settle is a high-backed wooden bench.

clue.text: Note about work hat

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A note concerning working headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a sun helmet, the pith hat worn in the tropics.

clue.text: Added sage as an alternative

parts.note: other means additional or further, as in 'other reasons'
wise means sage, as in a sage remark

explanation.surface: Some sage was put in as a substitute herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb but is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in a different way or else, offering an alternative.

clue.text: Sort of book it's difficult to endorse

parts.note: hard means difficult
to back is to support or endorse

explanation.surface: A kind of book that is hard to put your name to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers, as opposed to a paperback.

clue.text: Dishonest copper for one; this isn't rare

parts.note: base means low and dishonourable
copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A crooked policeman, for instance, is all too common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Common metals such as iron and lead, as opposed to precious ones, are called base metals, so they are not rare.

clue.text: Example found to make actor repeat himself …

parts.note: a type is a representative example
to found metal is to cast it

explanation.surface: An instance is discovered of an actor having to play the same role again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered' but is the foundry verb meaning to cast. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Typecasting puts an actor in the same kind of part again and again.

clue.text: Some get hanky out to show appreciation

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people pull out a handkerchief as a mark of gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying words of gratitude is how one shows appreciation.

clue.text: Behaviour interesting police as former partner leaves county

indicators.note: something that leaves is taken out of the word

parts.note: Sussex is a county on England's south coast
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Conduct attracted police notice when an ex-partner quit the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word. SUS or SUSS is British slang for suspicion, as in the old 'sus law' letting police stop people on suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, suspicious behaviour that draws police attention is called suss.

clue.text: … in response to this?

parts.note: continuing the previous clue, the call from an audience that makes a performer repeat a piece

explanation.surface: An actor repeats himself in answer to some prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 17 Down: the actor repeats his performance in response to the audience's call.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience's call for a repeat performance is what makes a performer do it again.

clue.text: Born con man has marked accent

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for born in genealogies
a rogue is a dishonest rascal, a swindler

explanation.surface: A born swindler speaks with a strong accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish.

clue.text: Maxim for an international banker

definitions.meaning: the ... of Zurich, a jibe at Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A saying fit for a global financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. 'Gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s British jibe at Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is an aphorism, and Swiss financiers were nicknamed the gnomes of Zurich.

clue.text: Fancy diet many prove explosive

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A fad diet often proves to have dramatic effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prove' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is a high explosive invented by Alfred Nobel.

clue.text: Missions take time over appeals

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: asks means makes requests or appeals

explanation.surface: Missions take a while on top of requests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a job or assignment, which is what a mission is.

clue.text: Tile round pool

parts.note: tile and lid are both slang for a hat
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: Tiles arranged around a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old slang for a hat, as is 'lid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: She's apt to come belting down the aisle

definitions.text: She's apt to come belting down the aisle

parts.words: She's apt to come belting down the aisle
parts.note: reads like a bride racing to the altar, but describes a cabin crew member checking seat belts in a plane's gangway

explanation.surface: A bride is liable to race down the church aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belting' suggests speeding, but she is checking passengers have fastened their belts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin crew walk down the aircraft aisle making sure seat belts are fastened.

clue.text: Thrashed fee out in unfashionable case

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
the outer word acts as a case holding the other

parts.note: dated means out of fashion

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fee was knocked out in an old-fashioned legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lawsuit, but 'case' teams with 'in' as the container signal, and 'out' shuffles the fee to EFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrashed in a contest is to be soundly beaten.

clue.text: Get the last two to attend to come forward and sign up

indicators.note: the final pair of letters is the part that moves
the moving part is brought to the front of the word

parts.note: to attend is to listen, pay heed

explanation.surface: Ask the final pair to pay attention, step forward and join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' and 'and' are link words. Moving EN from the end of LISTEN to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join the armed forces, signing up for service.
